capabilities.target: user MFA methods and temporary access pass issuance
message containing temporary access pass to ticket requester

inputs.source: support tickets, including tickets emailed in by contractors and vendors

instructions.note: The prompt directs the agent to reset MFA and send the temporary pass to the requester based on ticket opening, without an independent identity-binding step to the account owner.
The safety condition is expressed in instruction text; only one declared structural gate is described.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in the queue tool
controls.decay_rationale: The analyst sees the raw action target, requester, and full ticket text in the queue tool before approving the reset. It does not decay with model capability, but effectiveness can degrade under approval volume and under autonomy changes that remove or narrow the gate.

controls.name: Bind temporary pass delivery to the account owner from system of record
Human approval gate on temporary pass delivery

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted ticket can trigger account reset and exfiltrate the temporary pass to the requester

attack_path.note: Contractors and vendors can author tickets by email; requester is the email sender.
Agent looks up the user named in the ticket.
Agent resets MFA after analyst approval.
Temporary pass is posted to the requester rather than the account owner.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

findings.residual_rationale: The only declared approval gate covers cap.mfa_reset, not the actual S3 sink cap.send_temp_pass. Under the rubric, no step-2 credit applies to the exfiltration sink, so the path remains at the inherent floor.

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in unattended execution or model version changes should trigger reassessment, but this path is already critical because the delivery sink is ungated.

evidence.observation: The prompt tells the agent to look up the user, reset MFA, and send the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, so ticket content and requester identity are untrusted.
The temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner.
The approval view is only described for idp.reset_mfa; no approval is described for chat.send_temp_pass.

recommendations.action: Deliver temporary passes only to the account owner or another identity-bound destination from the system of record, never to the ticket requester field.
Add a human approval gate to cap.send_temp_pass, with raw destination and payload review, until destination binding is enforced.

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): analyst-approved reset can be used to change another user's MFA based on an untrusted requester

attack_path.note: Requester identity comes from email sender and ticket body.
Reset operation changes MFA methods and issues a temporary pass for the named account.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval volume is about 400 requests per shift across two analysts; any increase in queue rate, any remembered approval mode, or removal/narrowing of the reset gate should trigger reassessment.

evidence.observation: The agent is instructed to reset MFA for MFA problems after looking up the user.
The queue shows the exact target account, requester, and full ticket body before approval, so the reset itself is gated by raw-action human review.
Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift; high volume creates approval-fatigue pressure even though the gate is structurally independent.
Contractors and vendors can open tickets, and requester identity is based on email sender rather than an independent account-owner verification step.

recommendations.action: Require identity verification bound to the account owner before cap.mfa_reset can be approved, rather than trusting the ticket requester field.

rating.rationale: Present risk is dominated by a TC1 path from untrusted emailed tickets to an irreversible restricted-data egress sink that is not covered by the declared approval gate. The reset gate materially narrows only the MFA-reset path, leaving temporary-pass delivery to the requester as a critical residual risk. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design, prompt text, approval view, and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, source code, or runtime enforcement artifacts were provided, so capability scope, credential scope, and whether chat.send_temp_pass is separately gated or destination-bound are assessed from the described design only.
No identity-verification workflow artifact was provided; the assessment therefore treats ticket requester identity as untrusted and not independently bound to the account owner.
